To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a decrease in the regulatory T cells correlates with overall survival after sunitinib therapy in metastatic renal cell cancer patients and in primary renal cell cancer neoadjuvant setting.

sunitinib treatment decreases regulatory T cells in peripheral blood and in tumors, and the decrease of peripheral blood regulatory T cells after sunitinib therapy correlates with overall survival in metastatic renal cell cancer.

the number of FoxP3+ regulatory T-cells decreases in the peripheral blood of metastatic renal cell cancer patients after sunitinib based antiangiogenic therapy and that a decrease of regulatory T-cells correlates with an improved overall survival of these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new markers of response to antiangiogenic therapy and the demonstration of its immunomodulatory effect in the tumor micro-environment.
the development of a new predictive marker for antiangiogenic therapy and provides new insight into the role of regulatory T cells and their modulation by antiangiogenic therapy.
the identification of new predictive and prognostic biomarkers for antiangiogenic therapy in renal cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decrease of regulatory T cell in peripheral blood is an independent prognostic factor for sunitinib based antiangiogenic therapy in metastatic renal cancer patients.
the number of regulatory cells in blood or tumor is predictive of response to sunitinib and may be a marker of overall survival in metastatic renal cell cancer patients.
the decrease of regulatory T cell number is associated with a better outcome in metastatic renal cell cancer patients treated with sunitib.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decrease in the number and function of regulatory T cells is an important predictive marker of sunitinibtreated metastatic renal cell cancer patients and that antiangiogenic therapy may reverse immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment.
antiangiogenic therapy is able to reverse immunosuppression and that this effect is correlated to clinical benefit.
the measurement of peripheral blood regulatory T cell number may be a useful biomarker for the evaluation of antiangiogenic response in metastatic renal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the number of regulatory CD3+CD25hiFoxp3+ T cells in blood or tumor is a good predictive marker of response to sunitinib and that the decrease of regulatory T cell number is a good prognostic factor for metastatic patients.
antiangiogenic therapy is able to reverse immunosuppression and that this effect is predictive of clinical response.
antiangiogenic therapy may be more efficient in patients with a high level of immunosuppression.
